result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers lead with the decision and consequence and keep content readable without a presenter. B is a bit better because it gives desk readers more to work with: the occupancy impact sits on slide 1 and slide 4 lays out the approve/don't-approve options in a table. It does put derived figures (84%, $468/acre) and an inferred 'expected to stay' into the slides, though it labels them as derived. A sticks more strictly to the supplied facts but is slightly sparser, with somewhat repetitive slides 1 and 4. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the $145,000 decision and the non-renewal consequence first. A gives a desk reader more to work with: a side-by-side approve/don't-approve table, a per-acre cost and the effect on leased share. B repeats the same three facts across slides 1, 2 and 4 and gives the committee little beyond them. A loses a point on item 5: it puts the 84% figure on slide 1 even though that figure depends on an unconfirmed assumption, and its $470 vs $468 per acre is inconsistent. B deliberately kept the 84% figure off the slides, so it is the stricter answer on figures.
